build.cpuBackend: interpreter (no dynarec — mupen64plus-next's new_dynarec is native-x86/ARM-only; see docs/research/n64-wasm-jit-plan.md, this is the Phase N0 baseline, not the final JIT track)
notes: Core's own emscripten Makefile block patched: -fno-common (Emscripten/Clang -fcommon archive-resolution quirk left plain globals like retro_thread undefined when pulled from a static archive), -pthread -matomics -mbulk-memory (GLideN64 ThreadedOpenGl needs shared-memory-linked objects compiled with atomics/bulk-memory, not just linked with -pthread), GLES3 := 1 (core defaulted to GLES2; switched to match RetroArch's HAVE_OPENGLES3=1 / WebGL2 target).

libretro-common/glsym/glsym_es3.c recompiled standalone with ~203 additional -D<name>=glupen_<name> renames (beyond the core's existing ~20-entry rename list) to resolve duplicate-symbol link errors against RetroArch's own compiled copy of the same file; the renamed .o was spliced into the core's .a via emar before final link.

wasm-ld has no --allow-multiple-definition / -z muldefs equivalent, and llvm-objcopy for the wasm target has no symbol-table editing support (--localize-symbol etc.) — both were tried and confirmed unavailable before the -D rename approach was used.

GLideN64 gDP.cpp LLETriangle::draw() patched (2026-07-26): non-shaded LLE triangles (RDP cmd 0x08/0x09, gDPTriFill/gDPTriFillZ) never wrote vtx->r/g/b/a at all — updateVtx() only assigned vertex colour under `if (_shade)`. In G_CYC_FILL cycle mode CombinerInfo::update() swaps the colour combiner for a pure shade-only program, so the fragment colour IS that never-written vertex shade (uninitialised stack -> solid black under wasm). Real RDP hardware ignores the combiner in FILL mode and writes SET_FILL_COLOR, which gDPFillRectangle() already reproduced for rectangles via gDP.rectColor but LLE triangles were missing. Fix: seed non-shaded vertices from gDPGetFillColor() when cycleType == G_CYC_FILL (white otherwise, matching the function's own `int r = 0xff` intent), plus value-initialise the local SPVertex array. Symptom fixed: pre-rdpq libdragon content (rdp_enable_primitive_fill + rdp_set_primitive_color + rdp_draw_filled_triangle, e.g. games/n64-scene) rendered correctly-shaped but solid-black triangles while its fill rectangles were correctly coloured.

Linked with the opt-in NJ1 JIT-spike libs (N64_JIT=1 + N64_JIT_CODEGEN_LIB/N64_JIT_FRAMEWORK_LIB from ~/n64-jit-spike/build-wasm-codegen), matching the previously-shipped binary — the shadow-differential harness in cached_interp.c references vr4300_jit_bridge.o, which in turn needs Play!'s CodeGen/Framework archives at link time. See docs/research/n64-jit-nj1-spike.md.

Linked with RWEBAUDIO_JS_LIBRARY=emscripten/library_libretrowebxr_rwebaudio.js (retroarch-rwebaudio.patch from github.com/kblood/psx-wasm-jit-libretro), replacing RetroArch's stock page-only AudioContext audio glue with a worker-safe one that calls globalThis.__libretroWebXRRuntime.pushAudio(). Without this override the first N64 link used the stock library_rwebaudio.js, which assumes a real window.AudioContext unavailable inside a dedicated Worker; this override is core-agnostic (implements RetroArch's standard RWebAudio* ABI) and was already required infra from the PSX build, just not the RetroArch checkout's default.
